snippets.snippet: USD/CHF comes under selling pressure on Thursday as a sharp rally in the Japanese Yen (JPY) weighs broadly on the US Dollar (USD), while the Swiss Franc (CHF) draws support from stronger-than-expected inflation and growth data. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.8070, down 0.75% on the day.

Switzerland's Q2 GDP expanded by 1.9%, its strongest quarterly growth in five years and above the 1.6% consensus. Swiss CPI rose 0.4% month-over-month in August and 0.8% year-over-year, easing deflation concerns.

The decline in USDCHF was primarily driven by a domestic inflation surprise in Switzerland, which prompted a swift repricing of Swiss National Bank policy expectations and fueled demand for the Swiss franc relative to the U.S. dollar. August CPI data showed headline inflation accelerating to 0.8% year-over-year, comfortably exceeding market expectations for a 0.5% gain.

USD/CHF drops below the 50-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) of 0.8090... The Relative Strength Index (RSI) turned bearish, an indication that sellers are in charge. Hence, in the short term, further downside is expected.
